findings.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — [P1 confidence=100 blocking] Applying `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` to every group truncates the public members screen to 50 users because its route calls `model.findMembers();` once and its template only renders `{{#each m in members}}`, while all pagination actions and controls exist exclusively in the admin controller/template, making members after the first 50 unreachable for ordinary visitors to custom groups that previously displayed their entire membership.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — [P1 confidence=100 blocking] Replacing the PATCH membership dispatcher and nested PUT payload with `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` makes existing `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` requests carrying `changes: {add: username}` return success without adding a member and set a visible group to invisible, while existing PUT requests carrying `group: {name: ..., visible: "true"}` likewise silently ignore their attributes and hide the group, so the still-routed API needs compatibility handling or an explicit rejection before changing persisted state.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — [P2 confidence=100 advisory] Using `Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json', {` couples membership identity to the draft name bound by `{{text-field name="name" value=name placeholderKey="admin.groups.name_placeholder"}}`, so an administrator editing group A's name to existing group B and then paging or adding a member replaces A's displayed membership/count with B's even though writes still target A through `this.get('id')`; the strongest rebuttal is that names are the public endpoint's established identifier, but independent membership actions now run before Save, so separating draft attributes from persisted identity or using an ID-based read is necessary and eliminates draft-name lookup dependencies from both mutation refreshes and page navigation.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — [P2 confidence=100 blocking] For groups with more than 50 members, `{{#each m in members}}` displays only the first page because `findMembers` now requests `limit: this.get("limit")` with a default of 50 and the public members route/template provides neither pagination controls nor a subsequent-page fetch, making the remaining members inaccessible through that page.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — [P2 confidence=100 blocking] `return Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1;` counts an extra page whenever a nonempty group contains an exact multiple of 50 members, so a 50-member group displays `1/2` and enables Next to fetch offset 50 and show an empty member list.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — [P2 confidence=100 advisory] Changing the member-list response to `render json: {` with `members: serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer)` and pagination metadata introduces an unverified read contract because the submitted tests exercise only Admin::GroupsController and none exercise GroupsController#members or the client consuming its response; when this contract changes, group-page users and maintainers lack a regression check for response shape, ordering, and page boundaries, and although the strongest rebuttal is that the new admin membership tests cover the feature, those tests only inspect database membership counts and never invoke this endpoint or deserialize its response.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — [P1 confidence=75 blocking] `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and the equivalent `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` discard the mutation promise without a rejection handler, so a failed PUT or DELETE leaves the administrator on the unchanged membership list with no operation error or retry state, unlike the existing save/delete actions that display failures.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — [P1 confidence=100 blocking] Both membership mutation callbacks invoke `self.findMembers();` without returning its promise, so a successful PUT/DELETE followed by a failed GET resolves the mutation as complete while the administrator continues seeing stale membership and the refresh rejection escapes the mutation's error chain.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:35 — [P1 confidence=100 blocking] `group.set("offset", offset);` commits pagination before `return group.findMembers();` succeeds in both navigation actions, so a rejected next-page request leaves the old members under the new page number and the following Next skips the failed page or remains disabled on the nominal last page.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — [P2 confidence=100 advisory] When an administrator clicks Next twice before the first response arrives, unconditional `self.setProperties({` and `offset: result.meta.offset,` let the older response overwrite the newer page and undo the last navigation; the strongest rebuttal is that normal navigation waits for a response, but neither navigation action has an in-flight guard or disables the links while loading, so the supported UI admits the reversing response order.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a breaking API change. Looking at the diff, the old code accessed params via `payload = params[:group]` and then `payload[:visible]`, `payload[:name]`, etc. The new code directly accesses `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`, etc. This means existing API clients sending `PUT /admin/groups/:id` with `{group: {name: 'x', visible: 'true'}}` will have their parameters ignored since the controller now expects flat params like `{name: 'x', visible: 'true'}`. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:107 — [P2 confidence=100 advisory] When administrators modify a populated group, the replacement membership specs fail to protect unrelated members because the add case starts empty and asserts only `group.users.count.should == 2` while the removal case starts with one member and asserts only `group.users.count.should == 0`, so replacing all memberships on add or deleting every membership on removal satisfies both tests; the strongest rebuttal is that these examples verify the requested happy-path mutations, but it does not address preservation of existing members, which the deleted incremental-add setup previously exercised, so seed an unrelated member and assert the exact surviving user IDs for both operations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test coverage gap in the new specs. Looking at the diff, the old incremental tests had setup that added a user first (`@user1 = Fabricate(:user); group.add(@user1)`) before testing additions, which verified existing members were preserved. The new `add_members` test creates an empty group and only asserts `group.users.count.should == 2`, which would pass even if the implementation replaced all members. Similarly, `remove_member` starts with one member and asserts count == 0. While these tests verify the happy path, they don't verify that existing unrelated members are preserved during add operations. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for the new code, though it's about test quality rather than a bug in the implementation itself.
